review.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
review.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. IMPLEMENTED IN ROUND 45, AND IT IS THE ONLY TASK IN THE RECOVERY CAMPAIGN THAT NEEDED NO PROVENANCE WORK AT ALL -- genuinely unstarted, so an ordinary start captures a true base. THE RULE IS STRUCTURAL, WITH NO REGISTRY VENDORED, exactly as the script rule already is. A new spokenLanguage helper answers which language will come out of the speakers rather than which subtag a string starts with, and it differs from primarySubtag in precisely one place: where a macrolanguage has been narrowed by an extended-language subtag. BCP-47 spells a language as 2*3ALPHA optionally followed by an extlang of exactly 3ALPHA, while a region is two letters or three DIGITS and a script is four letters, so three ASCII letters immediately after a two- or three-letter primary is unambiguously an extlang and nothing else can take that shape in that position. RFC 5646 permanently invalidates the second and third extlang positions, so there is at most one to find. THE COLLAPSE RUNS TOWARD THE SPECIFIC RATHER THAN THE GENERAL, which is what makes the equivalence clause work in both directions: zh-cmn becomes cmn rather than zh, so the prefixed and bare spellings of one language agree, and the equivalence survives any region or script suffix because those subtags are never consulted. A bare zh stays zh -- it names the macrolanguage and neither variety, so treating it as either would invent a preference the viewer did not express, which is the same asymmetry the script rule uses when it says a tag naming no script conflicts with nothing. THE NEW OUTCOME IS ITS OWN REASON, as the acceptance requires: preferred_language_other_variety_only, distinct from preferred_language_other_script_only and from the regional fallback, because the three have different remedies -- a script conflict is about READING and the dialogue is still the viewer's, a regional difference is cosmetic and is still selected, and this one is the wrong language. Reporting it as a regional fallback would move the defect out of the matcher and into the vocabulary. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING THAT THE DESIGN MADE TRUE BY ACCIDENT AND THE TESTS NOW PIN: the script and variety findings are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than merely ordered. matchesOnlyAcrossScripts requires a match under ignore_script, setting the script aside leaves the spoken-language comparison, and a different variety fails it -- so zh-yue-Hant against a zh-cmn-Hans preference is not across both boundaries, it is simply the wrong language and the script question is moot. Only a track in the viewer's own spoken language can be across the script boundary, which is the only case where a font is the remedy. EXERCISED THROUGH BOTH CONSUMERS, which the acceptance demands because the two share one comparator precisely so they cannot drift, and the way that guarantee fails is one being corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. selectAudioTrack is asserted not to hand a Mandarin listener a six-channel Cantonese track that would have won on quality had the language matched, and selectSubtitleTrack is asserted to refuse a Cantonese subtitle under the new reason while still returning it in ordered for a player to offer. TWO PROPERTIES HAD TO BE TIGHTENED RATHER THAN MERELY KEPT PASSING, and that is the most useful thing this task turned up. Both audio.property.test.ts and subtitles.property.test.ts asserted that a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which was a restatement of the rule being removed; once zh-cmn and cmn are both in languageTagArb it is simply false, since that is one spoken language with two primary subtags. Both now ask spokenLanguage, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher actually makes. The arbitrary gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
review.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck via npm run check, exit 0 under pinned Node 22 on the tree committed this round. spokenLanguage is derived from subtag SHAPE with no registry vendored, the same way scriptSubtag already is, so the new rule adds no data dependency to the package.

unit.evidence: vitest via npm run check, exit 0 on the tree committed this round. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers rather than through the helper, which the acceptance requires because the two share one comparator precisely so they cannot drift: selectAudioTrack is asserted not to hand a Mandarin listener a six-channel Cantonese track that would have won on quality had the language matched, and selectSubtitleTrack is asserted to refuse a Cantonese subtitle under its own new reason while still returning it in ordered for a player to offer. Equivalence is pinned in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one, and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix -- and a bare zh is refused against either variety, because it names the macrolanguage and neither. Shape confusion is pinned negatively: a region, a script, a variant and a private-use singleton are none of them read as an extlang. ONE EXISTING ASSERTION WAS REVERSED RATHER THAN ADDED TO, and it is recorded as such in the test: zh-cmn-hans-cn against zh-hant under ignore_script used to expect a match and now expects none, because that is exactly the conflation this task removes. TWO PROPERTIES WERE TIGHTENED. Both suites asserted a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which restated the rule being removed and is false once cmn and zh-cmn are both generated; both now assert spokenLanguage equality, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher makes. languageTagArb gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it.

PL-0902 adds 58 cases across stream-candidate.test.ts and stream-candidate.property.test.ts. THE DESIGN WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS CHOSEN: adding the field to streamCandidateSchema directly was tried and breaks typecheck in 11 files across 4 packages, none of them in this task's surface; that experiment was reverted before anything was written and is corroboration rather than the reason. The architectural reason is that streamCandidateSchema is the RANKER's input and DESKTOP_PLAYBACK section 4 rules that ranking may prefer a candidate only one adapter can play, so a score component discounting protected candidates would be a second opinion about routing living in the one component that must not hold one. Hence resolvedStreamCandidateSchema extends it and streamCandidateSchema is byte-for-byte unchanged. MUTATION-CHECKED FOUR WAYS, each caught and then restored: requiresContentDecryptionModule narrowed to === protected (3 failures), protection given a .default of clear (4), .strict() removed from the protected variant (2), and the licence URL allowed over http (2). Unknown is a MEMBER OF THE UNION rather than null or an absent field, deliberately -- null is the right spelling of unknown for a media fact, but every reader's reflex for a null DRM field is 'there is no DRM', and requiresContentDecryptionModule is written as state !== clear so a fourth state added later defaults to requiring a CDM rather than to a silent attempt. packages/contracts/src/testing/arbitraries.ts was NOT touched because PL-0206 is editing it; the generators are local to the property file and composed from the shared streamCandidateArb, with the follow-up named in the file.

review.title: DRM capability on the candidate and playback-session contract
review.description: packages/contracts/src contains no occurrence of drm, widevine, playready or eme -- verified by grep across the whole source tree on 2026-09-15. So a resolved candidate carries no statement about whether it is encrypted, under which system, or against which license server. PL-0901 makes that a blocking gap rather than a cosmetic one: the desktop build routes between an mpv adapter that has no CDM and cannot be given one, and a Shaka/EME adapter that has one, and PlayerAdapter.canPlay is required to return a REASON on both branches rather than a boolean guess. A reasoned decision cannot be made from a contract that carries no field to reason about, so this gates the capability routing in PL-0901 section 4.
review.notes: THE SHAPE IS A CAPABILITY DESCRIPTOR, NOT A BOOLEAN. An isDrm flag would answer the routing question and nothing else; the adapter also has to say WHY it refused, and a reason trail that says drm_required with no system named is not debuggable, which is invariant 4. The reviewer should expect at minimum the protection system and, where the boundary knows it, the license acquisition endpoint -- and should rule on whether an UNKNOWN encryption state is representable, because absent is not the same as none. A candidate whose encryption state was never established must not read as clear; that is the same required-and-nullable discipline PL-0207 established for media facts, and the precedent is deliberate. WHERE IT LIVES IS PART OF THE QUESTION. The descriptor could sit on streamCandidate, on the playback-session response, or on both with one deriving from the other. The candidate is what the ranker scores and the session is what the player is handed, and PL-0301's implementation already argues at packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/provider.ts that the playable address belongs on the session rather than the candidate, for a reason that may or may not extend to the key system. Settle it before writing it. NOTHING HERE MAY WEAKEN A PROTECTION. This task describes encryption so the correct player is chosen and so a refusal is explainable. It adds no decryption, no key handling and no fallback that would attempt a protected source with an engine that has no CDM -- invariant 2 -- and the mpv adapter's refusal must stay a refusal rather than becoming a degraded attempt. SEQUENCING: overlaps PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 on packages/contracts and must be sequenced after whichever is active. It should land before PL-0501 writes the session response, because retrofitting a discriminated field into a shipped contract is the change PL-0501's own acceptance warns about.
review.acceptance: A resolved stream candidate, or the playback session that carries it, states its content-protection requirement explicitly: the protection system where one applies, an unencrypted state that is asserted rather than inferred from an absent field, and an UNKNOWN state that is representable and does not read as unencrypted. PlayerAdapter.canPlay can decide routing from the contract alone, without inspecting a URL, a manifest or a provider-specific field, and can name the protection system in its refusal reason. Adding the field changes no existing candidate's meaning by accident: a candidate that omits it is refused by the schema rather than defaulted to clear. Provider-specific spellings stay inside @liberty/provider-sdk and are normalized before they reach the contract. No decryption, key handling or protection bypass is added.

The native case is proven by a TYPE-LEVEL literal rather than a fake adapter -- there is no NativePlayerAdapter yet, so no runtime path can produce one, and the literal fails tsc if engine_load_failed, the detail field, or the native-mpv engine id disappears. Three separate mutations were confirmed to fail tsc with exit 2.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head a074b986e899ba8b91d018c4bb71f8c12089b608, exit 0, 15 of 15 and 0 cached, 2172 passed. THE FINDING IS THAT TWO OF THE THREE MEMBERS WERE ALREADY ENGINE-NEUTRAL AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED: engine_load_failed is exactly 'libmpv did not load' and names no engine, no library and no host. The gap was never a missing member; it was that the union was DOCUMENTED as three observed browser situations, so a native adapter author would reasonably conclude none applied and invent one. So this is a re-specification plus the missing detail channel, not a new member -- and adding libmpv_unavailable beside browser_unsupported was refused, because that would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the coupling the task exists to remove. 'The engine loaded and refused this source' was also refused: unavailability is decided once before any source, while a per-source refusal is per-candidate and feeds failover, and DESKTOP_PLAYBACK section 3 already owns it as PlayerRefusalCode on canPlay. That refusal is what satisfies the no-retryable constraint BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard. CONSTRAINT PROVEN IN THREE LAYERS: the reason set and the failure-kind set are disjoint and neither contains network_transient; the live route was traced -- an unavailability does reach classifyPlaybackFailure as ENGINE_ERROR and returns null because describePlaybackError of a non-shaka error yields category null and code null -- and the detail's code is a namespaced STRING precisely so an mpv number cannot be assigned where the classifier reads Shaka's scale; and the unavailability state path terminates at fatal without touching the scheduler. Five mutations were each confirmed to fail, including collapsing the missing-engine case onto browser_unsupported and building the error from a Shaka timeout.

review.title: An engine-unavailable reason that can say libmpv did not load
review.description: EngineUnavailableReason in apps/web/src/components/player/playback-controller.ts is Shaka-shaped. Its members describe a browser that cannot run the web engine, and browser_unsupported is a misnomer the moment the engine is a native library in a desktop shell rather than a script in a page. There is no member that means the native player failed to load. A NativePlayerAdapter would have to report a false reason or invent one locally, and either makes the failure less debuggable than the web path it sits beside.
review.notes: THE VOCABULARY, NOT A NEW MEMBER. Adding a libmpv_unavailable member beside browser_unsupported would leave the union naming one engine's failure modes and one library's, which is the same coupling one layer up. The question for the reviewer is whether the reason should describe WHAT FAILED in engine-neutral terms -- the engine could not be loaded, the platform cannot run this engine, the engine loaded and refused this source -- with the engine's own detail carried beside it rather than encoded in the member name. COUPLED TO PL-0904 AND DELIBERATELY SEPARATE. Both are the same observation in two places: the player's error vocabulary assumes Shaka. They are separate tasks because they have different consumers -- unavailability is a startup decision the controller makes before any source is loaded, while a playback error is a per-attempt outcome the failover scheduler classifies -- and because merging them would put one review range across two behaviours. Whoever takes the second should read the first's verdict. DO NOT BREAK THE FAILOVER CLASSIFICATION. packages/media-engine consumes playback failures and treats network_transient as the only retryable class; an unavailability reason that leaks into that path as retryable would make the player retry a library that is not installed.
review.acceptance: The engine-unavailable vocabulary can represent a native engine failing to load without naming Shaka, a browser or libmpv in the member itself, and the existing web reasons keep their present meaning and their present tests. An engine's own detail is carried beside the reason rather than encoded in it. No unavailability reason reaches the failover scheduler as retryable. The rename or widening is proven by a regression that fails if browser_unsupported is reintroduced as the only way to say an engine is missing.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head a074b986e899ba8b91d018c4bb71f8c12089b608, exit 0, 15 of 15 and 0 cached, 2172 passed; 16 new cases, web suite 759 to 775 in its own worktree. THE ENGINE-SPECIFIC CODE IS NOT A FIELD BESIDE A TAG, IT IS INSIDE A VARIANT THE TAG UNLOCKS: a tag alone leaves error.code readable without anyone consulting it, while a discriminated union makes the narrow mandatory and the wrong read a build failure. Three independent barriers keep an mpv number off the classified fields -- code is typed as the literal null on the native variant, fault is a union so an unnarrowed read does not compile, and dispatch narrows on engine so the Shaka classifier cannot receive a native error. Mutation M4 is the one worth reading: it takes TWO simultaneous mutations to make an mpv 6 come back as rights_unverifiable, and the first barrier catches it alone. THE NATIVE BRANCH CLASSIFIES NOTHING AND THAT IS THE ANSWER RATHER THAN A STUB: stop and redirect are taken by aborted a branch up, what remains is an mpv error with no honest table, and the http-status branch was deliberately NOT written even though it would be engine-neutral, because mpv surfaces no HTTP status and the only way to produce one is parsing FFmpeg's English error text, which the failover contract forbids. PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. BOTH TEST FILES ARE APPEND-ONLY: git diff shows 149 and 90 insertions and ZERO deleted lines, so every pre-existing Shaka regression passes unmodified.

review.title: Playback errors carry an origin, so a native failure is not a Shaka number
review.description: PlaybackError in apps/web/src/components/player/shaka-error.ts carries code and category pinned to Shaka 5.2.x numbering. A native adapter has no such numbers: libmpv reports MPV_EVENT_END_FILE with a reason and an error field, on an entirely different scale. Today a NativePlayerAdapter must either report null in both fields, which discards the only diagnostic it has, or borrow a Shaka number that means something else, which is worse. PL-0901 requires the adapter boundary to expose recoverable and fatal errors without leaking an engine type, and this is where that leaks.
review.notes: AN ORIGIN, SO THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING. The proposal the desktop document records is that an error names the engine that produced it, and that its engine-specific code is read only in that origin's terms. The reviewer should also rule on whether the classification the failover scheduler consumes -- rights, decode, source_unavailable, network_transient -- stays engine-neutral and is derived per origin, which is the shape that keeps packages/media-engine from learning about either engine. AN HONEST CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED BEFORE IT IS DISCOVERED. mpv's END_FILE error is coarser than Shaka's code pairs, so a native origin will legitimately classify to unknown more often. The scheduler already handles that: an unclassified charged attempt cannot silently reset the budget, and attemptsByCandidate and attempt_failed_unclassified exist for exactly this. Do not manufacture a false classification to avoid the unknown branch -- PL-0204's approval turned on the budget being honest about what it could not classify. COUPLED TO PL-0903, SEPARATE FOR THE REASON RECORDED THERE.
review.acceptance: A playback error names the origin that produced it, and an engine-specific code is interpretable only against that origin rather than being read on one engine's numbering. A native error can be represented without borrowing a Shaka code and without discarding the detail the engine did supply. The classification packages/media-engine consumes stays engine-neutral, derived per origin, and unchanged in meaning for every existing Shaka case, proven by the existing shaka-error regressions continuing to pass unmodified. An error that cannot be classified stays unclassified rather than being assigned a plausible class.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Profile model
recommended.acceptance: Profiles are modelled above authentication rather than inside the auth library, with the active profile carried alongside the session rather than inside the identity record; profile scoping is present in the first migration rather than retrofitted, because that is the part that is expensive to reverse; profiles can be created and selected with authorization tests

recommended.title: Provider health contract
recommended.acceptance: A provider with zero observations reports unknown with a null observed success rate and a zero sample count, never a mid-range score and never a pass; any prior used to rank an unobserved provider is labelled as a prior rather than presented as measured availability; degraded-but-usable is a state distinct from up and down; health output is pure over the observations plus an explicit policy version, with no hidden wall-clock decay; and health never affects entitlement, so a provider at perfect health still cannot make an unauthorized candidate eligible

typecheck.evidence: turbo run typecheck --filter @liberty/provider-sdk exit 0 under pinned Node 22 resolved via npx node@22.

unit.evidence: turbo run test --filter @liberty/provider-sdk exit 0 under pinned Node 22: zero observations yielding unknown with a null observed rate and a zero sample count, a prior labelled rather than presented as measurement at the same ranking number as a measured value, the degraded band held distinct from up and down, purity over observations plus an explicit policy version with Date.now replaced by a thrower to prove no wall clock is read, whole-report permutation invariance under generated policies, monotonicity in each count, and a compile-time guard that no health type can carry entitlement.
